actions.name: Exploit Log4Shell for initial access to unpatched VMware Horizon server

evidence.quote: In February 2022, the threat actors exploited Log4Shell [T1190] for initial access [TA0001] to the organization’s unpatched VMware Horizon server.

actions.name: Establish connection to known malicious IP address 182.54.217[.]2

evidence.quote: As part of their initial exploitation, CISA observed a connection to known malicious IP address 182.54.217[.]2 lasting 17.6 seconds.

actions.name: Run PowerShell command that added an exclusion tool to Windows Defender

evidence.quote: The actors’ exploit payload ran the following PowerShell command [T1059.001] that added an exclusion tool to Windows Defender [T1562.001]

actions.name: Observe HTTPS activity from IP 51.89.181[.]64 to VMware server

evidence.quote: Specifically, CISA observed HTTPS activity from IP address 51.89.181[.]64 to the organization’s VMware server.

actions.name: Observe suspected LDAP callback on port 443 to IP 51.89.181[.]64

evidence.quote: Following HTTPS activity, CISA observed a suspected LDAP callback on port 443 to this IP address.

actions.name: Observe DNS query for us‐nation‐ny[.]cf resolving to 51.89.181[.]64 during Log4Shell LDAP callback

evidence.quote: CISA also observed a DNS query for us‐nation‐ny[.]cf that resolved back to 51.89.181[.]64 when the victim server was returning this Log4Shell LDAP callback to the actors’ server.

actions.name: Gain access to VMware service account with administrator and system level access

evidence.quote: By exploiting Log4Shell, the actors gained access to a VMware service account with administrator and system level access.

actions.name: Add exclusion tool allowlisting entire c:\drive to enable downloading tools without virus scans

evidence.quote: The exclusion tool allowlisted the entire c:\drive, enabling threat actors to download tools to the c:\drive without virus scans.

actions.name: Download mdeploy.text from 182.54.217[.]2/mdepoy.txt to C:\users\public\mde.ps1

evidence.quote: The exploit payload then downloaded mdeploy.text from 182.54.217[.]2/mdepoy.txt to C:\users\public\mde.ps1 [T1105].

actions.name: Execute mde.ps1 to download file.zip from 182.54.217[.]2 and remove mde.ps1 from disk

evidence.quote: When executed, mde.ps1 downloaded file.zip from 182.54.217[.]2 and removed mde.ps1 from the disk [T1070.004].

actions.name: file.zip contained XMRig cryptocurrency mining software and configuration files

evidence.quote: file.zip contained XMRig cryptocurrency mining software and associated configuration files.

actions.name: Install XMRig on VMware Horizon server

evidence.quote: After obtaining initial access and installing XMRig on the VMWare Horizon server

actions.name: Create Scheduled Task named RuntimeBrokerService.exe to execute RuntimeBroker.exe daily as SYSTEM

evidence.quote: The exploit payload created a Scheduled Task [T1053.005] that executed RuntimeBroker.exe daily as SYSTEM.
The Scheduled Task was named RuntimeBrokerService.exe to masquerade as a legitimate Windows task.

actions.name: Use RDP and built-in Windows user account DefaultAccount to move laterally to VMware VDI-KMS host

evidence.quote: the actors used RDP [T1021.001] and the built-in Windows user account DefaultAccount [T1078.001] to move laterally [TA0008] to a VMware VDI-KMS host.

actions.name: Download around 30 megabytes of files from transfer[.]sh server associated with 144.76.136[.]153 on VDI-KMS host

evidence.quote: Once the threat actor established themselves on the VDI-KMS host, CISA observed the actors download around 30 megabytes of files from transfer[.]sh server associated with 144.76.136[.]153.

actions.name: Download PsExec, Mimikatz, and Ngrok tools

evidence.quote:
The actors downloaded the following tools: 
• PsExec – a Microsoft signed tool for system administrators. 
• Mimikatz – a credential theft tool. 
• Ngrok – a reverse proxy tool

actions.name: Execute Mimikatz on VDI-KMS to harvest credentials

evidence.quote: The threat actors then executed Mimikatz on VDI-KMS to harvest credentials
The threat actors then executed Mimikatz on VDI-KMS to harvest credentials and created a rogue domain administrator account [T1136.002].

actions.name: Create rogue domain administrator account

evidence.quote: The threat actors then executed Mimikatz on VDI-KMS to harvest credentials and created a rogue domain administrator account [T1136.002].

actions.name: Use newly created rogue domain administrator account to leverage RDP to propagate to several hosts

evidence.quote: Using the newly created account, the actors leveraged RDP to propagate to several hosts within the network.

actions.name: Manually disable Windows Defender via GUI on each host

evidence.quote: Upon logging into each host, the actors manually disabled Windows Defender via the Graphical User Interface (GUI)
Upon logging into each host, the actors manually disabled Windows Defender via the Graphical User Interface (GUI) and implanted Ngrok executables and configuration files.

actions.name: Implant Ngrok executables and configuration files on multiple hosts

evidence.quote: Upon logging into each host, the actors manually disabled Windows Defender via the Graphical User Interface (GUI) and implanted Ngrok executables and configuration files.
The threat actors were able to implant Ngrok on multiple hosts to ensure Ngrok’s persistence should they lose access to a machine during a routine reboot.

actions.name: Proxy RDP sessions via Ngrok, observable as outgoing HTTPS connections to tunnel.us.ngrok[.]com and korgn.su.lennut[.]com

evidence.quote: The actors were able to proxy [T1090] RDP sessions, which were only observable on the local network as outgoing HTTPS port 443 connections to tunnel.us.ngrok[.]com and korgn.su.lennut[.]com

actions.name: Establish deep foothold and move laterally to domain controller

evidence.quote: Once the threat actors established a deep foothold in the network and moved laterally to the domain controller

actions.name: Execute PowerShell command on Active Directory to obtain list of all machines attached to domain

evidence.quote: they executed the following PowerShell command on the Active Directory to obtain a list of all machines attached to the domain [T1018]

actions.name: Change password for local administrator account on several hosts

evidence.quote: The threat actors also changed the password for the local administrator account [T1098] on several hosts as a backup should the rogue domain administrator account get detected and terminated.

actions.name: Attempt to dump LSASS process with task manager

evidence.quote: the threat actor was observed attempting to dump the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS) process [T1003.001] with task manager but this was stopped by additional anti-virus the FCEB organization had installed.
